title: Prefetch-Fallback Coordinator: design notes and rollout checklist (WIP)
content:
Context and objective:
This document captures a proposed design for a small runtime component we call the Prefetch-Fallback Coordinator (PFC). PFC sits between request routing and the low-level kernel executor and has three co-equal goals:

1) Increase throughput and predictability by orchestrating KV-cache prefetches and batch scheduling for long-running chats.
2) Enable safe, low-latency speculative decoding paths that can be torn down quickly on mismatch or policy triggers.
3) Provide deterministic rollback/acceptance signals when onboarding new model variants or kernel combos (quantized, fused kernels).

Why a coordinator?
We currently have pieces (kvcache, batching, kernel selector, fallback rules) implemented as mostly independent modules. The coordinator is a lightweight policy layer that: 1) centralizes prefetch decisions to avoid redundant preload work, 2) exports clear instrumentation (per-request signals) for model integration, and 3) authoritatively decides when to route requests to fallback variants (cheaper quantized model, CPU-path, or prior stable model).

High-level responsibilities
- Maintain a short-lived request context for each active session (chat or scoring session) with: sequence length histogram, recent kvcache hit/miss ratio, last kernel used, and active prefetch tokens.
- Apply policies to decide: prefetch token prefixes, prefetch concurrency budget per-GPU, speculative decode enablement, and fallback activation.
- Act as the source of truth for variant rollouts: track canary populations, escalate errors to rollout manager, and trigger automated rollback when thresholds crossed.
- Offer an API for kernels to report warmup metrics and for the observability stack to consume coordinator signals.

Key design concepts
1) Handoff tokens and prefetch hints
- Each request can optionally include a prefetch_hint (prefix tokens that are likely to be used next). Hints come from higher-level chat logic (client SDK, policy engine, or previous-turn heuristics).
- Coordinator aggregates hints for the same shard/GPU and batches prefetches to avoid duplicated KV loads. Aggregation window is tunable (default 8ms) to not increase tail latency.
- Handoff tokens are assigned a TTL and a weight (importance). Low-weight hints may be dropped under pressure.

2) Speculative decode paths (two-tier model strategy)
- Fast path: quantized, fused-kernel variant with lower memory and compute. Provides speculative token stream.
- Verifier path: full-precision or larger variant used to verify and finalize outputs.
- Coordinator decides per-request whether to start both paths in parallel (speculative) or only fast path. Decision factors: client-specified latency SLO, user-tier, cost budget, and recent mismatch rate for that session.
- When verifier validates a speculative prefix, the coordinator issues the commit. If mismatch detected, coordinator triggers patching logic: either re-decode the suffix on verifier or use a fallback merge strategy (token-level reconciliation).

3) Kernel selection handshake and warmup
- Kernels expose a small handshake API: accept(request_profile) -> {expected_latency_ms, preferred_batch_size, warmup_needed}. Coordinator uses this to pick kernels that match current sequence length distribution.
- Warmup signals are scheduled through the coordinator before assigning requests. Warmup is prioritized by projected request value (SLAs, revenue tier) and cross-tenant fairness rules.

4) KV-cache consistency and invalidation rules
- Each model variant (including quantized/compiled build) owns a version tag for KV cache entries. When switching variants we use "stale-kv detection": a checksum on cached KV chunks is verified on first use; mismatch triggers proactive eviction for affected shards.
- Coordinator coordinates cross-shard invalidation to avoid thundering herds: it issues invalidation tokens and staggers evictions using a leaky-bucket backoff.

Acceptance and rollout workflow (draft)
- Preconditions: unit tests, perf benching, and model-level evals (quality delta against golden prompts) are green.
- Canary stage (1-2% of traffic): PFC flags canary population, speculative decoding may be disabled by default for initial canary. Metrics collected at 10s granularity.
- Progressive rollout: increase weight in phases (5%, 20%, 50%, 100%) with at-least-one-day stability windows. Coordinator exposes rollout_state and will auto-pause growth if thresholds exceeded.

Automated rollback triggers (examples)
- Latency: p95 increase > 30% over baseline for a 1-hour window.
- Cost: per-token compute cost > 1.3x baseline for a sustained window (accounting for speculative duplication).
- Quality: normalized BLEU/ROUGE/perplexity degradation over evaluation prompt-set > configured delta (example: perplexity +18%). Also track "regression on critical prompts" that are treated as hard gates.
- KV health: sustained KV miss-rate increase > 5% and cache churn > 2x baseline indicating cache incompatibility.
- Error spikes: 5xx increase > 3x baseline or new error codes introduced by kernel path.

On rollback
- Coordinator will immediately stop routing new requests to the failing variant and redirect existing sessions to fallback stable variant.
- Eviction pattern: mark in-flight kvcache entries as 'draining' and avoid prefetching new entries for the rolled-back variant.
- Post-rollback diagnostics bundle is auto-generated and attached to the rollout ticket (includes per-request traces, kernel warmup metrics, token-level diffs for a stratified sample).

Metrics: what we instrument and why
- request_latency_ms: p50/p95/p99 split per-variant and per-kernel. (Why: detect tail regressions caused by speculative merges or kernel slow-paths.)
- kv_prefetch_hit_ratio: hits/(hits+misses) per-shard and per-session. (Why: quantify value of aggregated prefetches.)
- speculative_mismatch_rate: fraction of speculative prefixes that were changed by verifier. (Why: determines wasted compute and quality risk.)
- extra_token_cost_rate: additional token compute due to speculative duplicates (tokens decoded twice) normalized by baseline tokens. (Why: cost attribution for billing and optimization.)
- kernel_warmup_time_ms: time between scheduling warmup and warm kernel becoming operational. (Why: informs warmup budget tuning.)
- rollback_frequency and rollback_cause: discrete event logs for post-mortem.
- per_prompt_regression_count: number of prompts in monitoring set that regressed beyond threshold. (Why: safety gate for quality.)

Data schemas (simple)
- coordinator_signal: [request_id, session_id, variant_id, kernel_id, prefetch_hint, speculative_enabled_bool, decision_timestamp_ms] serialized to our events pipeline.
- mismatch_event: [request_id, sample_tokens, speculative_prefix, verified_prefix, cost_delta_tokens, time_to_patch_ms].

Scheduling algorithm sketch
- Inputs: inbound request queue, per-GPU prefetch budget B_g, recent batch latency profile by kernel, pending warmups W, priority queue for sessions.
- Algorithm (greedy with backpressure):
  1) Pop up to N requests from queue where N is limited by GPU free slots and kernel preferred batch sizes.
  2) For each session, decide prefetches: score = f(SLO_weight, session_kv_miss_rate, hint_weight). Prefetch if score > threshold and prefetch budget left.
  3) If speculative allowed and predicted verifier cost < abort_threshold, spawn speculative job on fast path while scheduling verifier at lower priority.
  4) Enforce per-GPU concurrency caps and fair share across tenants.
  5) Monitor backpressure: if verifier queue grows beyond safety, automatically reduce speculative rate by halving speculative probability for affected sessions.

Privacy and multi-tenant isolation
- Cache entries are namespaced by tenant_id and variant_id. Coordinator enforces metadata checks to ensure no cross-tenant reads. Prefetch aggregation groups by tenant first, then shard to avoid leaking correlation across tenants.

Operational runbook (short)
- If p95 increases and speculative_mismatch_rate > 10%: immediately toggle speculative=off via the coordinator feature flag; observe cost and latencies for 30 minutes; if errors persist, rollback variant.
- If kv_prefetch_hit_ratio drops sharply: reduce prefetch window and inspect hint sources (client SDK or policy engine) for regressions.
- For kernel warmup failures: temporarily drain requests to that kernel and run a targeted kernel health job that replays sampled in-flight sessions as synthetic traffic.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- How aggressive should speculative decoding be for free-tier clients vs. paid customers? (tiered policy seems appropriate but we need numerical thresholds)
- Should mismatch patching prefer re-decode-on-verifier or token-level reconciliation? Re-decode is simpler but more costly; reconciliation is complex correctness-wise.
- Prefetch aggregation window: 8ms default reduces redundant work but may add tail latency; we should run A/B tests to find sweet spot per-region.
- Is checksum-based stale-kv detection sufficient for compiled-operator changes or do we need higher-fidelity provenance (compiler build ids + layer checksums)?

Immediate next steps
- Implement minimal coordinator prototype that supports prefetch aggregation + per-request signals (2-week spike).
- Add instrumentation for speculative_mismatch_rate and kv_prefetch_hit_ratio (1 week).
- Plan a small canary where speculative decoding is off for canary, then progressively enable for tiered traffic (work with product & SRE).

Notes to self / TODOs
- Draft a confluence page summarizing rollout matrix and attach sample dashboards.
- Coordinate with solutions-eng to get a set of 200 critical prompts for per_prompt_regression_count.
- Follow up with kernel team on warmup handshake API: define exact proto.

Appendix: quick pseudocode for mismatch handling
- on_speculative_finish(req): store speculative_prefix; enqueue verifier_job(req)
- on_verifier_finish(req): if verifier_prefix.startsWith(spec_prefix): commit(spec_prefix + verifier_suffix) else: if cheap_reconcile_possible(spec_prefix, verifier_prefix): reconcile_tokens() else: re_decode_from_last_common_prefix()

This doc is intentionally a working draft. Feedback welcome, especially from kernel and kvcache owners on warmup costs and invalidation semantics.
